request.system: You assist requirements analysts who apply the OGORE framework. You refine one IT goal of an organization's Initial Goal Tree Model by adapting validated goal patterns retrieved from a Goal Knowledge Base. Use only the six OGORE element types: Goal, Task, Resource, Actor, Belief, Constraint. Do not invent KPI values.

messages.content:
RETRIEVED PATTERNS:
[SKB-04/G2] (similarity 0.5308)
PATTERN SKB-04 | regional bank back office (synthetic) | financial services; zero-trust access to transaction systems
Organization goal: protect customer transactions against unauthorized access and change
IT goal G2: Every access request verified (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Requests authenticated and authorized per request (target 100%); G2-K2 Privileged sessions with multi-factor authentication (target 100%)
  Tasks: Authenticate each request against the identity provider; Evaluate access policy per request (role, device, context); Require step-up authentication for privileged actions
  Resources: Identity provider; Policy decision point
  Actors: IT Security Officer; Branch Staff
  Beliefs: No network location is trusted by default
  Constraints: Shared accounts are not permitted
  Rational statement: Per-request verification removes the implicit trust that let compromised sessions move laterally.
  Conflict resolved: per-request policy checks added latency to teller screens -> cache policy decisions for 5 minutes for non-privileged reads; privileged actions always re-verified

[SKB-03/G3] (similarity 0.5206)
PATTERN SKB-03 | online retailer (synthetic) | e-commerce; customer personal data protection
Organization goal: earn customer trust by protecting personal data
IT goal G3: Data subject requests fulfilled (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G3-K1 Requests closed (target within 30 days)
  Tasks: Register and verify each data subject request; Export or erase the customer's data
  Resources: Request register
  Actors: Data Protection Officer; Customer Service Agent
  Beliefs: none
  Constraints: Identity is verified before any data is released

[SKB-01/G2] (similarity 0.4802)
PATTERN SKB-01 | medium-sized food and beverage distributor (synthetic) | wholesale distribution; order-to-cash and lot traceability
Organization goal: deliver complete and traceable orders to retail customers
IT goal G2: Customer orders recorded accurately (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Order lines matching the customer purchase order (target 99.5%); G2-K2 Order confirmation sent after entry (target within 30 minutes)
  Tasks: Capture customer purchase order with price list validation; Confirm order to customer
  Resources: Customer price list; Order management module
  Actors: Sales Administrator; Customer
  Beliefs: Price lists are customer specific
  Constraints: A confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request
  Conflict resolved: lot scanning slows picking and delays confirmation -> confirm the order at entry and scan lots at picking, so confirmation time is unaffected

[SKB-07/G2] (similarity 0.4757)
PATTERN SKB-07 | hospital pharmacy (synthetic) | medicine handling; expiry and dispensing control
Organization goal: dispense safe medicines without waste from expiry
IT goal G2: Expiry dates controlled (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Items picked first-expiry-first-out (target 100%); G2-K2 Expired items removed from stock (target within 1 day of expiry)
  Tasks: Record batch and expiry at receipt; Suggest picking by earliest expiry; Report items expiring within 90 days
  Resources: Pharmacy stock module
  Actors: Pharmacist in Charge; Pharmacy Technician
  Beliefs: Regulation requires batch records for every medicine
  Constraints: Only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines
  Rational statement: Batch and expiry captured at receipt make both FEFO picking and recalls possible.

QUERY:
GOAL: G05 "Access to order, stock, and contract data verified for every request (zero trust)"; parent G01 "Regulated order-to-delivery controlled and secure"
DOMAIN: pharmaceutical distribution to hospitals; organization type: medium-sized distributor with an order portal and an LLM-based ordering assistant
KPIS: G05-K1 = Requests authenticated and authorized per request (100%); G05-K2 = Privileged actions protected by multi-factor authentication (100%); G05-K3 = Quarterly access reviews completed (100%)
ACTORS IN SCOPE: Hospital Buyer; Sales Administrator; Responsible Pharmacist; Quality Assurance Officer; IT Security Officer; Data Protection Officer; AI Product Owner
BELIEFS: No network location, including the office network, is trusted by default
CONSTRAINTS: Shared accounts are not permitted

TASK: (1) Rank the retrieved patterns by relevance to the query and state why each is relevant, citing its pattern ID. (2) Adapt them to the query and propose Tasks, Actors, Resources, Beliefs, and Constraints for the goal (and sub-goals only if the goal needs further decomposition). (3) Link every proposed element to the goal ID or to one of its KPI IDs, exactly as given in the query. (4) Draft one rational statement that explains how the goal and its elements serve the parent goal and its KPIs. (5) Give, for each element, the pattern ID it was adapted from; if it was not taken from a retrieved pattern, write UNGROUNDED. Every proposed element must respect the beliefs and constraints listed in the query.

ranked_patterns.relevance: Highest relevance: it is the same IT goal type (per-request verification under zero trust) with near-identical KPIs (authenticated/authorized per request 100%, MFA on privileged sessions 100%), the same belief that no network location is trusted by default and the same constraint banning shared accounts. Its tasks (authenticate against the identity provider, evaluate access policy per request, step-up authentication), resources (identity provider, policy decision point) and its recorded conflict resolution (short-lived caching of non-privileged read decisions, privileged actions always re-verified) transfer directly to G05 in the pharmaceutical distributor's order portal.

Second: it supplies the identity-verification-before-release constraint and the register/traceability mechanics for handling requests from external parties, which map to hospital buyers using the portal and the LLM assistant, and it introduces the Data Protection Officer, an actor in scope for G05. Its request register pattern is reusable as the access review register needed for G05-K3.

Third: same regulated medicine-handling sector. It contributes the regulatory belief that traceable batch records are required (extended here to records of who accessed or changed order, stock and contract data) and the constraint that only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines, which defines a privileged action requiring MFA under G05-K2, plus the Responsible Pharmacist actor.

Fourth and weakest: it is about order recording accuracy rather than access control, but it shares the order-to-cash scope and supplies the Sales Administrator and Customer (Hospital Buyer) actors and the constraint that a confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request, which identifies order amendment and price-list changes as privileged actions to be protected under G05-K2.

elements.text: Entitlements to order, stock and contract data reviewed and kept current
elements.justification: G05 needs one decomposition step because KPI G05-K3 (quarterly access reviews) addresses the lifecycle of entitlements, which is not covered by the per-request verification tasks adapted from SKB-04/G2.

elements.text: Authenticate every request to the order portal, stock views and contract data against the corporate identity provider
elements.justification: Direct adaptation of 'Authenticate each request against the identity provider', scoped to the distributor's order, stock and contract data; it is the primary driver of the 100% authentication target.

elements.text: Evaluate the access policy for each request using role, device, location and request context before returning order, stock or contract data
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Evaluate access policy per request (role, device, context)'; authorization per request is the second half of KPI G05-K1 and enforces the zero-trust belief.

elements.text: Require step-up multi-factor authentication for privileged actions (amending a confirmed order, changing contract prices, releasing quarantined stock, changing entitlements)
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Require step-up authentication for privileged actions'; the privileged action list is specialised using the quarantine release rule of SKB-07/G2 and the order change rule of SKB-01/G2.

elements.text: Verify the identity of the hospital buyer before any order, stock or contract data is released through the portal
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Register and verify each data subject request'; external requests from hospital customers must be identity-verified before data release, supporting the 100% authorization target.

elements.text: Propagate the end-user identity to the LLM ordering assistant so that every assistant-initiated request is authorized under that user's entitlements
elements.justification: No retrieved pattern covers an AI assistant; the query's LLM-based ordering assistant would otherwise bypass per-request verification, so identity propagation is added to keep G05-K1 at 100%.

elements.text: Log every access decision (identity, request, decision, timestamp) for order, stock and contract data
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Record batch and expiry at receipt' as a record-at-source practice; an access decision log makes the KPIs measurable and supports regulated traceability of who saw or changed data.

elements.text: Run a quarterly review of roles and entitlements with the data owners and revoke unused or excessive access
elements.justification: KPI G05-K3 has no counterpart in the retrieved patterns; a periodic recertification task is required to reach 100% completed quarterly reviews.

elements.text: Record the outcome and approval of each access review in the access review register
elements.justification: Adapted from the request register mechanics of SKB-03/G3, reused to evidence that quarterly reviews were actually completed.

elements.text: Identity provider with multi-factor authentication
elements.justification: Reused resource from SKB-04/G2; it is the single authentication authority that also enables the step-up MFA measured by G05-K2.

elements.text: Policy decision point for order, stock and contract data
elements.justification: Reused resource from SKB-04/G2; per-request authorization decisions require a central policy decision point.

elements.text: Access decision and change log
elements.justification: Adapted from the pharmacy stock module's batch recording role; the log is the evidence base for regulated audits and for measuring all three KPIs.

elements.text: Access review register
elements.justification: Adapted from the 'Request register' resource; it holds the quarterly review items, owners and closure status.

elements.text: Ordering assistant gateway that enforces authentication and policy checks on LLM requests
elements.justification: Specific to the query's LLM-based ordering assistant; no retrieved pattern provides an equivalent component.

elements.text: IT Security Officer
elements.justification: Same actor as in SKB-04/G2; owns the zero-trust access policy, the identity provider and the MFA rules.

elements.text: Data Protection Officer
elements.justification: Taken from SKB-03/G3; reviews that entitlements to customer and contract data remain proportionate at each quarterly review.

elements.text: Sales Administrator
elements.justification: Taken from SKB-01/G2; performs order and price-list actions that are classified as privileged and therefore require MFA.

elements.text: Hospital Buyer
elements.justification: Adapted from the 'Customer' actor of SKB-01/G2; the external requester whose portal and assistant requests must be verified per request.

elements.text: Responsible Pharmacist
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Pharmacist in Charge'; the only role allowed to perform quarantine release, a privileged action protected by MFA.

elements.text: Quality Assurance Officer
elements.justification: In scope in the query but absent from the patterns; validates that access reviews and access logs satisfy GDP/regulatory audit expectations.

elements.text: AI Product Owner
elements.justification: In scope in the query but absent from the patterns; accountable for the ordering assistant honouring identity propagation and per-request authorization.

elements.text: No network location, including the office network, is trusted by default
elements.justification: Stated in the query and confirmed by SKB-04/G2's belief; it is the rationale for verifying every request rather than trusting the perimeter.

elements.text: Regulation requires a traceable record of who accessed or changed order, stock and contract data
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Regulation requires batch records for every medicine' to the access-control context of a regulated pharmaceutical distributor.

elements.text: The LLM ordering assistant holds no entitlements of its own and always acts on behalf of an authenticated user
elements.justification: Needed to extend the zero-trust belief to a non-human requester introduced by the query; no pattern addresses AI components.

elements.text: Shared accounts are not permitted; every human and every service must use a named identity
elements.justification: Stated in the query and identical to SKB-04/G2's constraint; without named identities the per-request KPIs cannot be evidenced.

elements.text: Identity is verified before any order, stock or contract data is released
elements.justification: Reused constraint from SKB-03/G3, broadened from personal data to the regulated business data in scope of G05.

elements.text: Policy decisions may be cached for at most 5 minutes for non-privileged read requests; privileged actions are always re-verified
elements.justification: Adapted from the conflict resolution recorded in SKB-04/G2, which keeps portal response time acceptable for hospital buyers without weakening the MFA target.

elements.text: Only the Responsible Pharmacist may release quarantined medicines, and only after multi-factor authentication
elements.justification: Adapted from SKB-07/G2's release constraint, combined with the step-up authentication rule so that the regulated action counts toward G05-K2.

elements.text: A confirmed order cannot be edited without an authenticated change request by an entitled user
elements.justification: Adapted from SKB-01/G2's constraint; it defines order amendment as a privileged action subject to MFA and traceable approval.

output.rational_statement: Parent goal G01 requires the regulated order-to-delivery chain to be both controlled and secure, which only holds if no order, stock or contract record can be read or changed without a verified, named identity. G05 achieves this by verifying every single request instead of trusting the network it comes from: authentication against the identity provider and per-request policy evaluation drive G05-K1 to 100%, step-up multi-factor authentication on the privileged actions that materially affect delivery and compliance (order amendment, contract price change, quarantine release, entitlement change) drives G05-K2 to 100%, and quarterly entitlement reviews recorded in the access review register drive G05-K3 to 100% so that access rights do not drift between audits. Because the organization operates an order portal and an LLM-based ordering assistant, identity propagation through the assistant gateway keeps the assistant inside the same verification path rather than beside it. The access decision log supplies the traceability that regulated distribution and recall investigations expect, while the 5-minute caching rule for non-privileged reads keeps hospital buyers' portal response times acceptable without ever relaxing verification for privileged actions. All elements respect the query's belief that no network location, including the office network, is trusted by default, and the constraint that shared accounts are not permitted.
